claim.claim-text: CLAIMS:
1. A binding ligand comprising a targeting agent that binds to an aminophospholipid operatively attached to a therapeutic agent.
2. The binding ligand of claim 1, wherein said targeting agent comprises an anti- aminophospholipid antibody or antigen-binding fragment thereof.
3. The binding ligand of claim 2, wherein said targeting agent comprises an IgG or IgM anti-aminophospholipid antibody.
4. The binding ligand of claim 2, wherein said targeting agent comprises an scFv,
Fv, Fab', Fab or F(ab')2 antigen-binding region of an anti-aminophospholipid antibody.
5. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent comprises a monoclonal anti-aminophospholipid antibody, or antigen-binding region thereof.
6. The binding ligand of claim 5, wherein said monoclonal anti- aminophospholipid antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, is prepared by a preparative process comprising:

(a) preparing an anti-aminophospholipid antibody-producing cell; and
(b) obtaining an anti-aminophospholipid monoclonal antibody from said antibody-producing cell.

7. The binding ligand of claim 6, wherein said anti-aminophospholipid antibody- producing cell is a human patient's cell, wherein said patient has a disease associated with the production of anti-aminophospholipid antibodies.

8. The binding ligand of claim 6, wherein said anti-aminophospholipid antibody- producing cell is obtained by in vitro stimulation of a mixed population of human peripheral blood lymphocytes with an immunogenically effective amount of an aminophospholipid sample.

9. The binding ligand of claim 6, wherein said anti-aminophospholipid antibody- producing cell is obtained by immunizing a non-human animal with an immunogenically effective amount of an aminophospholipid sample.

10. The binding ligand of claim 9, wherein said anti-aminophospholipid antibody- producing cell is obtained by immunizing a transgenic mouse that comprises a human antibody library with an immunogenically effective amount of an aminophospholipid sample.
11. The binding ligand of claim 6, wherein said preparative process comprises:

(a) fusing said anti-aminophospholipid antibody-producing cell with an immortal cell to prepare a hybridoma that produces an anti- aminophospholipid monoclonal antibody; and
(b) obtaining said anti-aminophospholipid monoclonal antibody from said hybridoma.
12. The binding ligand of claim 6, wherein said preparative process comprises:
(a) immunizing a non-human animal with an immunogenically effective amount of an aminophospholipid sample;
(b) preparing a collection of antibody-producing hybridomas from the immunized animal;
(c) selecting from the collection a hybridoma that produces an anti- aminophospholipid antibody; and
(d) culturing the selected hybridoma to provide said anti- aminophospholipid monoclonal antibody.

13. The binding ligand of claim 12, wherein the immunized animal is a transgenic mouse that comprises a human antibody library and wherein said anti- aminophospholipid monoclonal antibody is a human monoclonal antibody.
14. The binding ligand of claim 6, wherein said preparative process comprises:

(a) obtaining the anti-aminophospholipid antibody-encoding nucleic acids from said anti-aminophospholipid antibody-producing cell; and
(b) expressing said nucleic acids to obtain a recombinant anti- aminophospholipid monoclonal antibody.
15. The binding ligand of claim 6, wherein said preparative process comprises:
(a) immunizing an animal with an immunogenically effective amount of an aminophospholipid sample;
(b) preparing a combinatorial immunoglobulin phagemid library expressing RNA isolated from the spleen of the immunized animal;
(c) selecting from the phagemid library a clone that expresses an anti- aminophospholipid antibody; and
(d) expressing the anti-aminophospholipid antibody-encoding nucleic acids from said selected clone to provide a recombinant anti- aminophospholipid monoclonal antibody.

16. The binding ligand of claim 15, wherein the immunized animal is a transgenic mouse that comprises a human antibody library and wherein the recombinant anti- aminophospholipid monoclonal antibody is a recombinant human monoclonal antibody.
17. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, comprising a human, humanized or part-human chimeric anti-aminophospholipid antibody, or antigen-binding region thereof.
18. The binding ligand of claim 1, wherein said targeting agent comprises an aminophospholipid binding protein or an aminophospholipid-binding fragment thereof.
19. The binding ligand of claim 18, wherein said targeting agent comprises a phosphatidylserine binding protein or a phosphatidylserine-binding fragment thereof.
20. The binding ligand of claim 19, wherein said targeting agent comprises an annexin or a phosphatidylserine-binding fragment thereof.
21. The binding ligand of claim 18, wherein said targeting agent comprises a phosphatidylethanolamine binding protein or a phosphatidylethanolamine-binding fragment thereof.
22. The binding ligand of claim 21, wherein said targeting agent comprises a kininogen or a phosphatidylethanolamine-binding fragment thereof.
23. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent comprises two, three or multiple aminophospholipid binding sites.
24. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent is a recombinant targeting agent.
25. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent binds to phosphatidylethanolamine.
26. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent binds to phosphatidylserine.
27. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent is attached to an anticellular or cytotoxic agent.

28. The binding ligand of claim 27, wherein said targeting agent is attached to a steroid, cytokine, antimetabolite, anthracycline, vinca alkaloid, antibiotic, alkylating agent, epipodophyllotoxin, DNA synthesis inhibitor, daunorubicin, doxorubicin or adriamycin.
29. The binding ligand of claim 27, wherein said targeting agent is attached to a plant-, fungus- or bacteria-derived toxin.

30. The binding ligand of claim 29, wherein said targeting agent is attached to an A chain toxin, bacterial endotoxin, lipid A moiety of bacterial endotoxin, ribosome inactivating protein, α-sarcin, gelonin, aspergillin, restrictocin, ribonuclease, diphtheria toxin or Pseudomonas exotoxin.
31. The binding ligand of claim 30, wherein said targeting agent is attached to ricin A chain or deglycosylated ricin A chain.
32. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent is attached to a coagulant.
33. The binding ligand of claim 32, wherein said targeting agent is attached to a human coagulation factor.

34. The binding ligand of claim 32, wherein said targeting agent is attached to a coagulation factor selected from the group consisting of Factor ll/lla, Factor Vll/VIIa, Factor IX/IXa, Factor X/Xa, a vitamin K-dependent coagulation factor that lacks the Gla modification, Russell's viper venom Factor X activator, thromboxane A2, thromboxane A2 synthase and α2-antiplasmin.

35. The binding ligand of claim 32, wherein said targeting agent is attached to a Tissue Factor, dimeric Tissue Factor, trimeric Tissue Factor, polymeric Tissue Factor, mutant Tissue Factor or Tissue Factor derivative.
36. The binding ligand of claim 35, wherein said targeting agent is attached to a truncated Tissue Factor.
37. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent is attached to a first and a second therapeutic agent.
38. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent is attached to multiple therapeutic agents.
39. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, wherein said targeting agent is directly attached to a therapeutic agent.
40. The binding ligand of claim 39, wherein said targeting agent is directly attached to a therapeutic agent by a direct covalent bond or via a chemical cross- linker.
41. The binding ligand of claim 39, wherein said targeting agent is directly attached to a therapeutic agent by expressing said binding ligand as a recombinant fusion protein.

42. The binding ligand of any one of claims 1 through 38, wherein said targeting agent is indirectly attached to a therapeutic agent via an antibody, or antigen binding region thereof, that binds to said therapeutic agent.

43. The binding ligand of claim 42, wherein said binding ligand is a bispecific antibody that comprises a first, targeting antibody, or antigen binding fragment thereof, operatively attached to a second antibody, or antigen binding fragment thereof, that binds to said therapeutic agent.

44. The binding ligand of claim 1, wherein said targeting agent is an antiphosphatidylserine antibody, or antigen binding fragment thereof, that is directly or indirectly attached to truncated Tissue Factor.
45. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, dispersed in a pharmaceutically acceptable formulation.

46. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, for use in delivering a therapeutic agent to an aminophospholipid expressed on the luminal surface of blood vessels of a vascularized tumor upon administration to an animal having a vascularized tumor.
47. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, for use in killing tumor vascular endothelial cells upon administration to an animal having a vascularized tumor.
48. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, for use in inducing coagulation in tumor vasculature upon administration to an animal having a vascularized tumor.
49. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, for use in destroying tumor vasculature upon administration to an animal having a vascularized tumor.
50. The binding ligand of any preceding claim, for use in treating cancer upon administration to an animal having a vascularized tumor.
51. Use of a binding ligand in accordance with any preceding claim in the manufacture of a medicament for treating cancer.
52. A pharmaceutical composition comprising a biologically effective amount of a binding ligand in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 50.
53. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 52, wherein said composition comprises two binding ligands that each bind to a distinct aminophospholipid.
54. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 52 or 53, wherein said composition is formulated for intravenous administration.
54. The pharmaceutical composition of any one of claims 52 though 54, wherein said composition comprises a second anti-cancer agent.
55. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 54, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is a chemotherapeutic agent, radiotherapeutic agent, anti-angiogenic agent or apoptosis-inducing agent.

56. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 54, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is an antibody-therapeutic agent construct comprising a targeting antibody, or antigen binding fragment thereof, that binds to a surface-expressed, surface-accessible or surface-localized component of a tumor cell, tumor vasculature or tumor stroma; said targeting antibody or fragment thereof operatively linked to a therapeutic agent.
57. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 56, wherein said second targeting antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, binds to tumor cell or tumor stroma component.

58. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 56, wherein said second targeting antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, binds to a surface-expressed, surface- accessible, surface-localized, cytokine-inducible or coagulant-inducible component of intratumoral blood vessels of a vascularized tumor.

59. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 58, wherein said second targeting antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, binds to a surface-expressed component of intratumoral vasculature selected from the group consisting of an aminophospholipid, endoglin, a TGFβ receptor, E-selectin, P-selectin, VCAM-1, ICAM-1, PSMA, a VEGF/VPF receptor, an FGF receptor, a TIE, αvβ3 integrin, pleiotropin, endosialin and an MHC Class II protein.

60. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 58, wherein said second targeting antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, binds to a surface-localized component of intratumoral vasculature selected from the group consisting of VEGF/VPF, FGF, TGFβ, a ligand that binds to a TIE, a tumor-associated fibronectin isoform, scatter factor/hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), platelet factor 4 (PF4), PDGF and TIMP.
61. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 56, wherein said second targeting antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, is operatively linked to a cytotoxic agent.

62. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 56, wherein said second targeting antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, is operatively linked to a coagulation
factor or to an antibody, or antigen binding fragment thereof, that binds to a coagulation factor.

63. The pharmaceutical composition of claim 54, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is a naked antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, that binds to an aminophospholipid on the luminal surface of blood vessels of the vascularized tumor.
64. The pharmaceutical composition of any one of claims 52 though 63, wherein said composition is intended for human administration.
65. Use of a pharmaceutical composition in accordance with any one of claims 52 though 64 in the manufacture of a medicament for treating cancer.
66. A kit comprising a biologically effective combined amount of a binding ligand in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 50 and a second anti-cancer agent.

67. A kit comprising a biologically effective amount of a binding ligand in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 50 in combination with a diagnostically effective amount of a targeting agent-detectable agent construct that comprises a detectable agent operatively attached to a second targeting agent that binds to an aminophospholipid.

68. A kit comprising a pharmaceutical composition in accordance with any one of claims 52 though 64 in combination with a diagnostically effective amount of a
targeting agent-detectable agent construct that comprises a detectable agent operatively attached to a second targeting agent that binds to an aminophospholipid.
69. The kit of claim 67 or 68, wherein said targeting agent-detectable agent construct comprises the X-ray detectable compound bismuth (III), gold (III), lanthanum (III) or lead (II).

70. The kit of claim 67 or 68, wherein said targeting agent-detectable agent construct comprises the detectable radioactive ion copper67, gallium67, gallium68, indium111, indium"3, iodine123, iodine125, iodine131, mercury197, mercury203, rhenium186, rhenium188, rubidium97, rubidium103, technetium99"1 or yttrium90.

71. The kit of claim 67 or 68, wherein said targeting agent-detectable agent construct comprises the detectable nuclear magnetic spin-resonance isotope cobalt (II), copper (II), chromium (III), dysprosium (III), erbium (III), gadolinium (III), holmium (III), iron (II), iron (III), manganese (II), neodymium (III), nickel (II), samarium (III), terbium (III), vanadium (II) or ytterbium (III).

72. A method for treating an animal having a vascularized tumor, comprising administering to said animal a therapeutically effective amount of at least a first binding ligand that comprises at least a first therapeutic agent operatively attached to a targeting agent that binds to an aminophospholipid on the luminal surface of blood vessels of a vascularized tumor.

73. A method for imaging a vascularized tumor, comprising administering to an animal having a vascularized tumor a diagnostically effective amount of at least a first
binding ligand that comprises a detectable agent operatively attached to a targeting agent that binds to an aminophospholipid on the luminal surface of blood vessels of the vascularized tumor, and detecting the image of the tumor so formed.
74. A method for treating cancer, comprising:

(a) forming an image of a vascularized tumor by administering to an animal having a vascularized tumor a diagnostically effective amount of a targeting agent-detectable agent construct that comprises a detectable agent operatively attached to a targeting agent that binds to an aminophospholipid on the luminal surface of blood vessels of the vascularized tumor, thereby forming a detectable image of the tumor vasculature; and

(b) subsequently administering to said animal a therapeutically effective amount of at least a first targeting agent-therapeutic agent construct comprising a therapeutic agent operatively attached to a targeting agent that binds to an aminophospholipid on the tumor blood vessel luminal surface and thereby destroys the tumor vasculature.

75. A method for treating cancer, comprising simultaneously or sequentially administering to an animal having a vascularized tumor a therapeutically effective combination of a targeting agent-therapeutic agent construct comprising a therapeutic agent operatively attached to a targeting agent that binds to an aminophospholipid on the luminal surface of blood vessels of the vascularized tumor and at least a second anti-cancer agent.
